newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat gains extended on Egypt, acreage, funds.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat gains extended on Egypt, acreage, funds.

text.p: Gains were extended in CBOT soft red winter wheat futures on talk Egypt was seeking 500,000 tonnes of wheat and on ideas that U.S. SRW wheat acreage would be reduced, traders said.
At 1105 CST May was in fast trading and fund buying led the way up, the traders said.
"Smith Barney, Dean Witter and Refco are buying the July," a trader said.
Reports circulated that Egypt was seeking 500,000 tonnes of wheat for May shipment but Australia was expected to be a leading contender for the business.
Talk of a cut in U.S. wheat acreage was widespread amid strong rallies in soybean prices which led to ideas that wheat acres would be plowed up and soybeans seeded.
Also, talk continued that some wheat acres were destroyed by the floods in the U.S. Ohio River Valley. But agronomists have said there were not many acres of SRW wheat in the flooded areas.
At 1107 CST, wheat was 1-1/2 to seven cents per bushel higher, with March up 1-1/2 at $3.82-1/2 a bushel and May was up 6-1/2 at $3.88-1/2.
